_scope: Phase 9A — deterministic evaluation of the ingestion pipeline output. Inspects the built Chroma vector store (chroma_db/) rather than re-running ingestion — making this offline, network-free, and safe. Every expected value was verified against the actual live store before being recorded. Ingestion re-runs may produce slightly different chunk counts if upstream CSULB pages change content; expected_min/expected_max bounds are sized to absorb minor page edits without false failures while still catching structural regressions.
_source: Hand-curated. All min/max bounds and exact counts verified by inspecting the live chroma_db/ store via rag/store.load_vector_store()._collection.get() calls. chunk_id c31caccf_0000's duplication count (7) was first discovered and documented in Phase 8A — the eval here tracks it as a known characteristic of the current store state, not a new finding.

cases.description: Total chunk count is within a sane range. The live store has 491 chunks across all page types. A floor of 200 catches catastrophic ingestion failures; a ceiling of 1500 catches unexpected over-ingestion (e.g. a crawler running amok). These bounds absorb minor page content changes while catching structural regressions.

FAQ page type has at least 50 chunks. The live store has 98 FAQ chunks. FAQ is the highest-volume page type — a count below 50 indicates the FAQ page failed to ingest or chunking broke for this page type.

Deadlines page type has at least 5 chunks. The live store has 14 deadlines chunks — one per program (from the specialist _parse_deadlines_page() extractor) plus preamble text. A count below 5 means the deadlines specialist extractor failed and the program-isolated chunks were not produced.
Eligibility page type has at least 5 chunks. The live store has 11 eligibility chunks. This page covers GPA requirements and eligibility criteria — a common retrieval target.
Application process page type has at least 5 chunks. The live store has 19 application_process chunks — a modest count but sufficient for step-by-step guidance queries.

Program application page type has at least 100 chunks. The live store has 349 program_application chunks — by far the largest category, produced by dynamic discovery across all doctoral programs. A count below 100 means discovery failed or no program-specific pages were crawled.

Nursing (D.N.P.) program has at least 20 chunks. The live store has 44. Nursing is a priority program — a count below 20 means either the program seed URL failed or discovery found fewer subpages than expected.

Physical Therapy (DPT) program has at least 40 chunks. The live store has 94 — the largest single program. Physical Therapy has a richer program site with multiple subpages; a count below 40 indicates substantial crawl failure for this program.
Educational Leadership (Ed.D.) program has at least 50 chunks. The live store has 108 — the most heavily crawled program. A count below 50 indicates most of the discovered subpages were not ingested.

Engineering & Computational Mathematics (Ph.D.) program has at least 20 chunks. The live store has 75. Engineering is a common query target — very low counts would suggest the engineering doctoral studies page was not crawled.
Public Health (DR.P.H.) program has at least 10 chunks. The live store has 28. Public Health has a smaller web presence than other programs but should still produce meaningful coverage.

At least 5 distinct named programs are present in the knowledge base. The live store has 5 named programs (Nursing, Physical Therapy, Educational Leadership, Engineering, Public Health). A count below 5 means one or more programs were entirely missing from the crawl.
All 491 chunks have a non-empty url field. URL is required for source attribution — any chunk with a missing URL cannot be cited and will produce empty citation data in responses.

All chunks have a non-empty chunk_id field. chunk_id is required for the Phase 8A duplicate detection metric and for cache-busting logic. A missing chunk_id indicates a regression in rag/chunking.py's _make_chunk_id().

All chunks have a non-empty page_type field. page_type is required for the filtered retrieval path (rag/retriever.py's where_filter) — a missing page_type would cause those chunks to never match a filtered query.
All chunks have a non-empty title field. title surfaces in retrieval results and is used by the response builder for source attribution.

No chunks have empty page_content. The chunker strips and skips empty chunks — any empty page_content would indicate a regression in rag/chunking.py that lets empty strings through. The live store has 0 empty chunks.

No chunk exceeds CHUNK_SIZE=500 characters. RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter's chunk_size bound should be enforced on every chunk. Chunks significantly larger than 500 chars would indicate the splitter changed behavior or the parameter was overridden.
Deadlines source URL is present in the store with at least 5 chunks. The deadlines page is critical for 'when is the deadline' queries. A missing or very low chunk count would break that query path.
FAQ source URL is present in the store with at least 50 chunks. The FAQ page is the highest-volume source and must be present for general knowledge-base queries.

Known duplicate chunk_id c31caccf_0000 appears exactly 7 times. This ID is produced by hash('https://www.csulb.edu/graduate-studies-csulb/article/programs-advisors-and-deadlines-doctoral')[:8] at chunk_index 0 — all 7 occurrences share the same URL but represent separate deadline entries from the specialist _parse_deadlines_page() extractor, which assigns index=0 to each program card. This is a KNOWN, pre-existing structural characteristic of the deadlines specialist extractor first documented in Phase 8A. The case PASSES when the count is exactly 7 — a change in either direction signals an unexpected store state change.
